concepts.def: A sex cell, the sperm in males and the egg (ovum) in females, that fuses with another gamete at fertilisation to form a zygote.
The fusion of a sperm nucleus with an egg nucleus to form a diploid zygote, which then divides to form an embryo.
The roughly 28-day cycle in which the uterus lining thickens and an egg is released, controlled by hormones.
A hormone produced by the ovaries that repairs and thickens the uterus lining and triggers a surge of LH leading to ovulation.
A hormone from the pituitary gland that causes an egg to mature in the ovary and stimulates the release of oestrogen.
A fertility treatment in which eggs are fertilised by sperm outside the body and a resulting embryo is placed into the uterus.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Reproduction & Fertility — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Reproduction & Fertility brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Reproduction & Fertility.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Fertilisation in humans is the fusion of:
options: a sperm nucleus and an egg nucleus
two egg cells
two sperm cells
an egg and a body cell

mcqs.q: Which hormone stimulates an egg to mature in the ovary?
options: FSH
progesterone
testosterone
insulin
release of an egg from the ovary
fusion of sperm and egg
breakdown of the uterus lining
fertilisation of the egg
fertilising eggs with sperm outside the body
cloning an adult cell
preventing the egg from being released
fertilising the egg inside the ovary
A sperm nucleus fuses with an egg nucleus to form a diploid zygote, combining genetic material from both parents.
Fertilisation is just the sperm reaching the egg's surface.
Fertilisation is the release of an egg from the ovary.
FSH is produced by the ovary rather than the pituitary.

mcqs.q: What does FSH do in the menstrual cycle?
options: Children inherit DNA only from the mother.
FSH causes the uterus lining to break down.
FSH from the pituitary gland stimulates an egg to mature in the ovary and triggers oestrogen production.
FSH is produced by the ovary rather than the pituitary.

mcqs.q: Do children of the same parents have identical DNA?
options: Children of the same parents have identical DNA.
Fertilisation is the release of an egg from the ovary.
Children inherit DNA only from the mother.
No - gametes vary because of meiosis and random fertilisation, so siblings (except identical twins) differ genetically.
